bull_bear.body: Priority on high-value business segments (CDMO, Biologics, Peptides) to drive long-term growth. Debt/EBITDA targeted to remain stable or soften despite gross debt increase for capex. ROCE improved to 17.7% from 9.7%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruptions impacting raw material availability/logistics (near-term OTIF pressure); Solvent price volatility; Execution risk on large greenfield capex (Unit 7, Fermentation); Regulatory audit outcomes (though 132 audits passed without critical findings in FY26); Potential lumpiness in quarterly CDMO earnings despite annual growth.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and aggressive on capex; transparent about margin drivers; defensive on customer concentration (denies destocking risks); focused on 'strategic partnership' model over tactical; emphasizes scale and technology platforms (biocatalysis, continuous manufacturing).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Fermentation expansion initially targeting non-pharma/industrial chemicals (surfactants, polymers) to de-risk yield/contamination before pharma scale-up; CDMO definition strictly excludes generic CMO revenues; ARV absolute sales expected to remain flat (~INR 2,800 cr) while % mix shrinks; Peptide capex described as 'large' but specific numbers withheld.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Reinvestment-led allocation: capex ran at 19% of sales in the quarter (₹394 Cr), well above the FY22-27 average of 16%, funded alongside a deleveraging balance sheet.
- Net debt to EBITDA has been reduced from 3.4x in Q2 FY25 to 1.3x, giving headroom to keep funding growth capex internally.
- Asset turn ratio (ATR) sits near 1.0x and management guides to improvement in the medium term back in line with the five-year long-term average of above 1.0x, framing capex discipline in return terms.
- R&D is being treated as a growth investment, with spend at 5.8% of revenue including ₹35 Cr of capitalised R&D directed at advanced biologics (gene therapy and ADC).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated one-stop platform spanning clinical-stage development to commercial manufacturing across Affordable Medicines and CDMO
- Global leadership position in select APIs (ARV, oncology, cardiovascular, gastro) with backward-integration capability
- Scale and regulatory reach: 15 manufacturing sites globally accredited by USFDA, WHO, EMA and others, operated under a single quality standard for all markets
- R&D depth: 6 R&D sites, 3,134 scientists/quality-team strength, 244 patents granted, 94+ DS/DP launches, and technology platforms across flow chemistry, biocatalysis, fermentation and peptides
- Diversified, broad-based CDMO pipeline of 125+ active projects across human health, animal health and crop science, reducing customer/program concentration
- 20 years of industry track record with a global customer base of 275+ clients across 61 countries
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict disrupting trade, energy costs and supply chains — The Middle East war involving the US, Israel and Iran (which began February 28, 2026) caused India's exports to West Asia to fall 57.95% in March 2026; management flags this conflict as a source of sharply higher crude oil prices, disrupted energy supply and pressure on input costs and raw-material availability going into FY27.
- Rising trade protectionism and tariffs on exports — FY26 brought heightened uncertainty in global trade and the imposition of high, punitive tariffs by key trading partners on India; fluctuating trade policies are cited as a continuing source of uncertainty for the operating environment.
- Macro growth deceleration — India's GDP growth is projected to decline from an estimated 7.6% in FY26 to 6.9% in FY27, with management citing heightened uncertainty and rising economic risk tied to the Middle East conflict and its effect on energy infrastructure in Gulf nations.
- General business-continuity / operational risk exposure — The Board's Report references a Risk Management framework intended to recognise, evaluate and mitigate 'various foreseeable threats' across business segments amid an evolving external environment, but explicitly directs readers to a detailed risk discussion elsewhere in the Integrated Annual Report that is not included in this bundle.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Improve utilisation and expand the product portfolio in the API/Affordable Medicines business while strengthening participation across developed and emerging markets
- Drive closer integration between APIs and formulations to support reliable supply, cost competitiveness and faster execution
- FDF: deepen position in ARV formulations while building a calibrated portfolio in select molecules; progress product filings/approvals, expand oral solid dosage (OSD) capacity, and add products under CMO to improve utilisation
- Execute the KRKA joint-venture formulations platform to support access to regulated markets
- Small Molecules CDMO: deepen strategic customer partnerships, invest in differentiated technology platforms (biocatalysis, flow chemistry, trickle-bed processing, peptides), and expand development/manufacturing capacity
- Bio CDMO: build a diversified pipeline, scale fermentation capacity, strengthen downstream processing infrastructure and enzymatic-technology capability, and deepen long-term customer partnerships
- Group-wide: deepen strategic customer relationships, advance technology-led capabilities, expand commercial capacity and maintain quality/execution standards across the development-to-commercialisation cycle
- Reinvestment-led: the Company continues to direct capital toward capacity and technology expansion, including the newly allotted Laurus Pharma Zone land in Anakapalli District (projected multi-phase investment over eight years) and ongoing investment programmes across small molecule, fermentation, peptides and gene therapy/ADC platforms; capex intensity is expected to increase over FY27-28 to support these growth projects. Alongside reinvestment, the Company follows a policy of returning capital to shareholders through interim dividends (1st and 2nd interim dividends declared for FY26), while the strategic narrative emphasises 'ARV de-risking' via a rising CDMO revenue share and maintaining a strong balance sheet to fund the capex programme.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Laurus continued to expand its integrated manufacturing platform during FY26, anchored in Visakhapatnam (API, drug substance and finished-dosage facilities), complemented by fermentation capabilities in Bengaluru, development infrastructure in Hyderabad, and cell-therapy manufacturing through associate ImmunoACT in Mumbai. Capital allocation remained focused on growth-oriented API and CDMO manufacturing expansion; FY26 capex was ₹1,070 crore (16% of revenue), taking cumulative capex from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 to over ₹4,350 crore. Key ongoing/recently completed projects: (1) commercial-scale peptides manufacturing - several peptide synthesisers were installed and qualified during the year along with purification and isolation capabilities; (2) client-specific CMO oral dosage capacity, which became operational during the year, supported by an additional packaging line, with the full commercial production line expected to start from June 2026; (3) the Vizag microbial fermentation facility, with Phase 1 capacity of around 400 KL planned, on track for operations by end-2026; (4) a Gene Therapy/ADC cGMP facility in Hyderabad (groundbreaking June 2025) built for plasmid DNA, viral vectors (e.g. AAV), bioconjugation, lyophilisation and sterile fill-finish, with planned investment in the site of over ₹200 crore and expected completion by end-2026; (5) commercial spray-drying capability, identified as one of the capability additions within the FY26 manufacturing build-out; and (6) the KRKA JV FDF facility, with construction going as per plan and Phase-1 manufacturing blocks expected to be ready by mid-2027.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global pharmaceutical industry growth (9.3% in 2025) driven by chronic-disease prevalence, R&D investment, rising healthcare expenditure and broader access to medicines
- Global generics market growth (est. 6.5% CAGR to USD 770.0 billion by 2033) driven by patent expiries and sustained demand for affordable medicines
- Global small-molecule CDMO market expansion (USD76.1bn in 2025 toward ~USD145.5bn by 2035) driven by rising outsourcing and development complexity
- Global industrial biotechnology and precision-fermentation markets expanding rapidly, supporting the Bio CDMO opportunity set
- Customers rebalancing sourcing networks to reduce geographic concentration, positioning India (and Laurus) to benefit from supply-chain diversification
- Near-term FDF performance may continue to reflect procurement cycles and product-mix dynamics, though underlying demand environment remains resilient
- Tender cycles, pricing dynamics and approval timelines may continue to influence near-term phasing in the FDF business
- Bio CDMO: discussions for longer-term manufacturing contracts progressing, improving revenue visibility into FY 2026-27 and beyond
- Vendor diversification, rising chemistry complexity and customer preference for strategic end-to-end partners continue to support the small-molecule CDMO opportunity
- Small Molecules CDMO: active pipeline of more than 125 projects, including over 102 in human health and around 23 in animal health and crop science
- Bio CDMO: building a diversified pipeline across customers, applications and fermentation platforms, with continued pipeline progress on larger global accounts
- FDF: cumulative product dossier filings reached 94, with 7 dossiers filed and 6 approvals received during FY26

deepdive.thesis: Laurus Labs accelerated its transformation in FY26 with CDMO revenue crossing INR 2,000 crores (+38% small molecule) and EBITDA margins expanding to 26.8%, driven by commercial NCE launches and operational leverage. Management guided for aggressive capex of INR 3,000 crores over the next two years to double down on large-scale fermentation, peptides, and greenfield units, targeting a 50% CDMO revenue mix by 2030 while maintaining steady absolute ARV sales.

open.item: The Board-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement - demerger of Laurus Synthesis Private Limited's Unit-1 into Sriam Labs Private Limited, and amalgamation of the remaining LSPL business into Laurus Labs - is pending NCLT (Amaravati Bench) approval; the merger process is expected to be completed by September 2026.
Commercial-scale peptide manufacturing block to be ready for commercial-scale validation during Q2 of FY27.
Construction of the Vizag microbial fermentation facility progressed through the year; Phase 1 capacity of around 400 KL is planned, with the project on track for operations by end-2026.
The fermentation manufacturing site at Vizag is progressing as planned, with operations expected to commence by the end of 2026.

The Gene Therapy/ADC cGMP facility in Hyderabad, following groundbreaking in June 2025, is expected to be completed by end-2026, built for plasmid DNA, viral vectors (e.g. AAV), bioconjugation, lyophilisation and sterile fill-finish; planned investment in the site is over ₹200 crore.
Fermentation greenfield site for Laurus Bio — Phase 1 to start by end of 2026.
Commercial-scale fermentation facility at Vizag — Phase 1 (a little over 400 kilolitres) expected operational towards the end of 2026.
Commercial-scale fermentation facility Phase 1 (~400 kilolitres) in Vizag expected to be operational (handy) by end of 2026.
Vizag large-scale fermentation facility (with Eight Roads partnership) to more than double fermentation capacity and be ready by end of calendar year 2026.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected around 25% to 26% (standalone ~25%).
Confident of maintaining gross margin around 60% despite solvent price pressure.
Positive/good CDMO growth expected in FY27 over FY26 (CDMO FY26 ~Rs 2,080 cr), with year-on-year growth despite quarter-on-quarter lumpiness and no single-program concentration risk.
ARV revenue (Rs 2,800 cr in FY26) to remain constant in absolute terms (~Rs 2,500 cr +/- 300) while its percentage of total revenue declines going forward.
Affordable Medicines (Generics) division (FY26 Rs 4,733 cr, +18%) expected to continue strong growth in FY27 with order book in place (no quantitative guidance).
Gross debt (net debt Rs 2,285 cr, 1.25x EBITDA) may rise slightly in FY27, but debt/EBITDA to be maintained at similar or softening levels.
Animal Health to see good contribution in FY27 (some meaningful API shipments already); Crop Science needs a couple more financial years to ramp meaningfully.
Confident of maintaining or improving the current ~29% (Q4) EBITDA margin in FY27; operating leverage expected to play out over the next 2 years.

New large greenfield manufacturing project (Unit 7) — first production ready for commercial validation by March 2027, with four additional manufacturing blocks in FY28 (combined reactor volume over 2,000 cubic meters).
Majority of FY27 CDMO division revenues expected to be commercial supplies (vs clinical/late-stage).
CGT (viral vector/gene therapy) capex plus opex over the next 3 years could be close to Rs 300 crore, contingent on clinical trial progress.
